According to the World Bank, hydrocarbons accounted on average for 13% of GDP, 83% of exports and 46% of budget revenues over 2020–2024. Growth reached 4.1% in 2023, driven by public investment and household consumption.

Selon la Banque mondiale, le pétrole représente environ 20 % du PIB, 60 % des recettes fiscales et 95 % des exportations. Après la récession de 2016–2020, la croissance a repris en 2021 mais reste sensible aux cours du brut (3,1 % en 2025).
economyDesc.en: Angola is one of the two largest crude oil producers in Sub-Saharan Africa. According to the World Bank, oil accounts for around 20% of GDP, 60% of government tax revenues and 95% of exports. After the 2016–2020 recession, growth resumed in 2021 but remains sensitive to oil prices (3.1% in 2025).

La croissance est restée robuste, à 7,5 % en 2024 et environ 8 % sur les trois premiers trimestres de 2025 selon la Banque mondiale. economyDesc.en: Benin's economy is driven by services (trade, transport, the port of Cotonou), agriculture (cotton) and a growing industrial base. Growth remained robust at 7.5% in 2024 and about 8% over the first three quarters of 2025 according to the World Bank. The country is a marginal hydrocarbon producer (Sèmè offshore field) and hosts the export terminal of the Niger–Benin pipeline.

name: Egypt

C'est un producteur majeur de gaz naturel (champ Zohr) et un pôle régional de raffinage et de GNL. Selon la Banque mondiale, la croissance du PIB réel a atteint 5,3 % au premier semestre de l'exercice 2025/26, le secteur extractif restant freiné par les arriérés dus aux opérateurs.
economyDesc.en: Egypt is a diversified economy anchored by agriculture, manufacturing and services, as well as the Suez Canal. It is a major natural gas producer (Zohr field) and a regional refining and LNG hub. According to the World Bank, real GDP growth reached 5.3% in the first half of FY2025/26, while the extractive sector remained constrained by arrears owed to operators.

economyDesc.en: Equatorial Guinea is an economy heavily dependent on hydrocarbons (oil, Punta Europa LNG). According to the World Bank, the economy has declined over the past decade due to reduced oil output, contracting by 5.4% in 2025 after 0.4% growth in 2024. The country is seeking to monetise its gas resources and diversify its economy.

economyDesc.en: Gabon is a long-standing Central African oil producer whose public revenues remain closely tied to oil. According to the World Bank, growth accelerated to 3.4% in 2024 (2.4% in 2023), driven by large infrastructure projects and increased petroleum extraction. Over the medium term the country is banking on manganese, timber and iron ore to offset gradually depleting reserves.

The country is a net oil importer with a synthetic-fuels industry (Sasol, PetroSA) and its economy is constrained by electricity security, Eskom's energy availability factor having risen from 55% in 2023 to 63% in 2024.
